Q: How to reduce MoE (Mixture of Experts) inference cost with dynamic expert selection? A:

You can use **Adaptive-K routing** which dynamically selects the number of experts based on routing entropy.

## The Key Insight

When the router softmax distribution has **low entropy**, it means the router is confident about which expert(s) to use → fewer experts are sufficient.

When entropy is **high**, the router is uncertain → use more experts to maintain quality.

## Implementation

```python

pip install adaptive-k-routing

from adaptive_k import AdaptiveKRouter

# Initialize with K options and entropy thresholds
router = AdaptiveKRouter(
    k_values=[1, 2, 4],        # Possible K values
    h_thresholds=[0.6, 1.2]   # Entropy thresholds
)

# Route based on router logits
k, indices, weights = router.route(router_logits)
# Low entropy (H < 0.6) → K=1
# Medium entropy → K=2  
# High entropy (H > 1.2) → K=4

Q: Meteor can't find package eta/core even though it is installed A:

Meteor's module resolution is unable to resolve the ES module. It has its own module system and does not fully respect all Node.js ES module resolution rules, especially for sub-path exports defined in package.json.

I recommend filing a bug report concerning the error.

As a stopgap, you can directly patch oidc-provider to use const { Eta } = require('eta') instead until Meteor supports ESModule.

The patch-package is perfect for this. Configure it to run automatically after npm install and apply the patch to the oidc-provider package in node_modules.

package.json

 "scripts": {
+  "postinstall": "patch-package"
 }

patch-package ties the patch to the specific oidc-provider version so you won't need to worry about the patch breaking on updates.

You can create a patch by running:

npx patch-package oidc-provider

Then edit the patch file to use the commonjs module import: patches/oidc-provider+9.6.0.patch

diff --git a/node_modules/oidc-provider/lib/views/index.js b/node_modules/oidc-provider/lib/views/index.js
index c6dc14f..adc48d6 100644
--- a/node_modules/oidc-provider/lib/views/index.js
+++ b/node_modules/oidc-provider/lib/views/index.js
@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
-import { Eta } from 'eta/core'; // eslint-disable-line import/no-unresolved
+const { Eta } = require('eta');
 
 import layoutTemplate from './layout.js';
 import loginTemplate from './login.js';

Q: First step in programming A:

I’d recommend starting with plain JavaScript first. TypeScript is definitely a great tool and it helps a lot in bigger projects, but when you’re still learning the basics, it can feel like extra complexity on top of learning programming itself. Once you’re comfortable with JavaScript and your project starts growing, then moving to TypeScript will make much more sense and you’ll actually appreciate the benefits.

Q: How to reserve a tcp local port? A:

The idea to reserve the port is to block the usage of this port for an outgoing connection. I mean if you have a potential service that will open for LISTEN the port 8080, if you don't reserve it, and the range of ports include this port, could conflict with a outgoing connection that randomly uses 8080 as "source port".

Q: Invoke-Command failed: WinRM cannot complete the operation A:

Check your WinRM proxy settings by running following cmd command: netsh winhttp show proxy

By default WinRM send messages directly and do not uses proxy (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winrm/proxy-servers-and-winrm) In my case on this one host where I had exactly the same issue with Invoke-Command (same error msg) proxy was configured. You can remove proxy or in this case reset WinRM configuration to default with the following cmd command: netsh winhttp reset proxy

That did the trick for me!
